literature.paper: Wang, Shen, Chen, Yang, Tao & Yan (2023), ICLR — Towards One-Shot Neural Combinatorial Solvers (cardinality-constrained portfolio case study)
literature.comparison_level: SAME-DATA / SAME-CARDINALITY predict-then-optimize comparison. Uses the authors' own snp500.csv (494 full-history S&P 500 members), the exact train 2018-2020 / test 2021 split, 120-trading-day horizon, K=20, long-only, full investment, rf=3%. Signal + solver are substituted (our MASTER/TFT/PatchTST mu + PSO/SA vs their LSTM mu + Gurobi/CardNN); objective is our mean-variance P-tradeoff, NOT their max-Sharpe. Reported OOS metric is realized annualized Sharpe (mu-rf)/sigma computed Wang-style from daily realized portfolio returns, so it is directly comparable to their Table 3 / Fig 5. NOT an exact-objective replication.
notes: FAIRNESS/UNITS: horizon scaling (automatic) scales historical mu AND Sigma by the forecast horizon H so they live on the same H-period scale as the transformers' raw H-day mu. Without it the model mu was inflated ~H-fold against a 1-day Sigma, so the nominal P meant a different risk aversion per model (P'/(1-P')=c*P/(1-P)); PatchTST's weights were then identical at P=0.2/0.5/0.8, i.e. it was solving pure max-return while Historical solved real mean-variance. Scaling both moments is a no-op for the Historical solution (H factors out of the objective), so this repairs units only.

FAIRNESS/CADENCE: moment_refit=match_models re-estimates the historical mu/Sigma exactly when the models are retrained (model_refit), instead of the previous 'expanding' mode that refreshed the baseline every week while the transformers stayed frozen at fit_end. Both sides now act on the same information set.

FAIRNESS/RISK-MATCHING: the P grid is widened to 11 points so `python benchmark/run.py risk-matched --dir <output_dir>` can report every model at the P whose REALIZED annualized volatility matches the baseline's. Residual mu-dispersion differences (PatchTST still ~4x Historical after the unit fix) mean an equal-P read is still not an equal-risk read; the risk-matched table is the one to quote.

FAIRNESS/MU-WINDOW: each model is scored against its OWN matched historical baseline, emitted as a `Historical@<L>` row where L is that model's conditioning window in trading days (L = rows + feature_depth - 1; see the All-Weather config for the derivation). Here MASTER -> Historical@67 (T_LOOKBACK 8 + max(WINDOWS) 60 - 1), TFT -> Historical@271 (seq_len 252 + FEATURE_LOOKBACK 20 - 1) and PatchTST -> Historical@336 (= seq_len). Supersedes the former moment_mu_lookback_periods=252, which pinned ONE baseline at 252 days: that was mismatched against ALL THREE models (-204/+19/-84 days), and most severely against MASTER, which reads 67 days but was compared to a mean over 3.8x more history. The correction reverses MASTER's verdict on this regime -- it now trails its matched baseline (0.75 vs 0.88) where it previously appeared competitive. The matched mu is recomputed at EVERY decision regardless of moment_refit. NB the baselines themselves span 0.88/0.98/1.43 Sharpe at 67/271/336 days, and Historical@336 alone beats the paper's LSTM+Gurobi (1.08): lookback length is doing as much work here as the model choice. Sigma is left expanding and is shared by every mu source, so it cannot tilt the head-to-head.

UNITS/ANNUALISATION: periods_per_year=2.1 (=252/120). Each stored portfolio return is a 120-trading-day return, so annualising the mean requires 252/120, NOT the 12 implied by decision_step_days=21. The superseded run used 12, inflating annualised return 5.7x (Historical showed 272%) and Sharpe by sqrt(12/2.1)=2.39x; that is the source of the long-standing wang_risk_sweep vs wang_sharpe_table discrepancy.

CAVEAT/OVERLAP: decision_step_days=21 with forecast_horizon_days=120 means holding periods overlap ~83%. The 7 decisions are roughly 2 independent observations, and wang_sharpe_table shows sharpe_std >= sharpe for EVERY model. This benchmark can support 'same range as their LSTM+Gurobi', never a ranking between our own models.
